pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/flow/ScreenNodeRow.tsx:62 Selecting a flow-graph node always smooth-scrolls the matching row because this explicit API option is not gated on the reduced-motion signal and is not overridden by the global CSS scroll-behavior reset, one of several realized gaps in this context alongside a selection state the pill primitive never exposes and a Scaffold button that silently does nothing.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/flow/ScreenNodeRow.tsx:62 An explicit behavior:'smooth' wins over the globals.css scroll-behavior:auto reset, and this file reads no reduced-motion signal, so the scroll still animates under the preference. The looping edge and pulse animations in FlowGraph and WidgetRect do honor the signal via motionSafe.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/accessibility/AccessibilityTab.tsx:38 The single-select InteractivePill (src/components/ui/InteractivePill.tsx:128-135) renders plain buttons with no aria-pressed, aria-selected or group role, and the selection is only an animated background and colour. The language, HUD context and breakpoint selectors in this context all inherit that gap.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/wbp-starter/WBPStarterPanel.tsx:44 The Scaffold button is disabled only while isRunning (line 112), so with an empty class it stays focusable and enabled, activation does nothing, and no message appears: a false affordance. The tablist itself does rove correctly through SubTabNavigation.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/flow/FlowGraph.tsx:101 The visible text is node.label, but the name begins with 'Select', so it neither equals nor begins with the visible label; UIBindingsTab.tsx:106 repeats this. Separately, the WBP input (WBPStarterPanel.tsx:68-83) has no aria-invalid or aria-describedby tying it to its error text.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/wbp-starter/WBPStarterPanel.tsx:85 A feature-owned alert region is created together with its text instead of the component requesting an announcement from a region that already exists.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/wbp-starter/WBPStarterPanel.tsx:84 The conditional mount makes the region arrive already populated, the case the technique says leaves each reader to interpret. This is the same construct as the live-region finding seen from the delivery-layer rule, with no recorded pairing at the site.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/flow/ScreenNodeRow.tsx:116 The hide is an unmount, which is the preferred rung, but AnimatePresence keeps the subtree mounted through a visual-only exit with no inert on it, so its run button stays tabbable while collapsing. The leak is limited to the exit window.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/data.ts:197 The score card renders this constant as a grade and picks its success colour from it (AccessibilityTab.tsx:78-85) with no measured source, rules or surfaces, so an unmeasured value reads as an audit result. The sub_ui tests do query by role and name, but the focus check is a className proxy and none asserts where focus lands.
